tier1.text: Each thyrohyoid pulls down the hyoid bone, a small U-shaped bone in the upper neck. When you swallow or speak, each thyrohyoid also lifts the larynx, or voice box. This front neck muscle runs from the thyroid cartilage, or Adam's apple, to the hyoid bone.

quotes.quote: A skeletal muscle belonging to the infrahyoid muscle group, located in the anterior part of the neck, with its origin on the thyroid cartilage and its insertion on the hyoid bone; it functions to depress the hyoid bone and elevate the larynx during swallowing and speaking.
quotes.citation: NCI Thesaurus (NCIt), National Cancer Institute, https://ncithesaurus.nci.nih.gov

quotes.quote: larynx: voice box, a short passageway connecting the pharynx and the trachea
quotes.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.
